record.paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
record.original_question: What is the Weihrauch degree of the task that, given a Player I winning strategy in the Wadge game for a function, produces a point of discontinuity of that function? The source further notes that a computable winning strategy is known to imply the existence of a computable point of discontinuity, but it is open whether there is a uniform argument establishing this.

evidence.quote: Open Question 18 (Nobrega & P. [35]). What is the Weihrauch degree of obtaining a point of discontinuity of a function from a Player I winning strategy in the Wadge game for it?
It is known that a computable winning strategy implies the existence of a computable point of discontinuity, but not whether there is a uniform argument to establish this.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in the Baire space $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with its product topology. For a (partial) function $f:\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}\to\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, the Wadge game $G(f)$ is played as follows. In each round, Player I plays one natural number, extending an input sequence $x\in\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, while Player II plays either a natural number, extending an output sequence $y\in\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, or a "pass" symbol. After $\omega$ rounds, Player II wins if either Player I's sequence $x$ does not lie in $\operatorname{dom}(f)$, or Player II's sequence $y$ is infinite and equals $f(x)$; otherwise Player I wins. It is a classical fact that $f$ is continuous on its domain iff Player II has a winning strategy in $G(f)$, and (in the effective version) Player I has a winning strategy in $G(f)$ iff $f$ is discontinuous at some point of its domain.

Weihrauch reducibility. Given multi-valued partial functions $F,G$ on $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, one says $F\le_{\mathrm W} G$ if there exist computable functionals $H,K$ such that for every $G$-realizer $g$, the map $x\mapsto K(x,g(H(x)))$ is a realizer of $F$. The induced equivalence classes are the Weihrauch degrees.

Problem. Determine the Weihrauch degree of the multi-valued problem
$$\mathsf{WadgeDisc}\;:\;\sigma \;\mapsto\; \{x\in\operatorname{dom}(f_\sigma) : f_\sigma \text{ is discontinuous at } x\},$$
where the input $\sigma$ is (a code of) a Player I winning strategy in the Wadge game for some function $f_\sigma$, and the output is any point at which $f_\sigma$ is discontinuous.

It is known that whenever such a winning strategy is computable, there exists a computable point of discontinuity for $f_\sigma$; the question asks whether this passage is uniformly Weihrauch-computable, and if so to identify its precise Weihrauch degree.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up subsequent work on the discontinuity problem and on game characterizations of lower cones in the Weihrauch lattice (Brattka's "The Discontinuity Problem"; Nobrega–Pauly's game characterizations), but none of the located sources explicitly compute the Weihrauch degree of producing a point of discontinuity from a Player I winning strategy in the Wadge game. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Discontinuity Problem (Brattka)
status_evidence.snippet: Player I has a winning strategy for f iff f is effectively discontinuous; paper characterizes effective discontinuity but does not compute the Weihrauch degree of extracting a discontinuity point from such a strategy.
status_evidence.claim: Related foundational results, but does not resolve the specific uniform/Weihrauch-degree question.

status_evidence.title: Game characterizations and lower cones in the Weihrauch degrees (Nobrega–Pauly)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces parametrized Wadge games to characterize lower cones in the Weihrauch lattice.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework in which the question is posed but does not answer it.
